verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              स पल्या वचनं श्रुत्वा धर्मयुक्तिसमन्वितम् । हर्षेण महता युक्तो वाक्यं व्याकुललोचनः ॥१॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira said Having acquired great power and great riches, and having obtained a long period of life, how many one succeed in shunning death?

verses.sanskrit: तं वै शाकुनिकं दृष्ट्वा विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा । स पक्षी पूजयामास यत्नात्तं पक्षिजीविनम् ॥२॥
verses.english: By which of these means viz., penances, or the performance of the various acts, or by knowledge of the Shrutis, or the application of medicines, can one succeed in avoiding decrepitude and death.

verses.sanskrit: उवाच स्वागतं तेऽद्य ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते । संतापश्च न कर्तव्यः स्वगृहे वर्तते भवान् ॥३॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old narrative of Panchashikha who was a Bhikshu in his practices and Janaka.

verses.sanskrit: तद्ब्रवीतु भवान् क्षिप्रं किं करोमि किमिच्छसि । प्रणयेन ब्रवीमि त्वां त्वं हि नः शरणागतः ॥४॥
verses.english: Once on a time, Janaka, the king of Videhas, questioned the great Rishi Panchashikha, who was the foremost of all persons conversant with the Vedas and who had all his doubts removed about the object and meaning of all duties.

verses.sanskrit: अरावप्युचितं कार्यमातिथ्यं गृहमागते । छेत्तुमप्यागते छायां नोपसंहरते द्रुमः ॥५॥
verses.english: The King said By what conduct, O holy one, may one get over Decrepitude and Death? Is it by penances, or by the understanding, or by religious practices, or by study and knowledge of the scriptures.

verses.sanskrit: शरणागतस्य कर्तव्यमातिथ्यं हि प्रयत्नतः । पञ्चयज्ञप्रवृत्तेन गृहस्थेन विशेषतः ॥६॥
verses.english: Thus addressed by the king of the Videhas the learned Panchashikha, conversant with all invisible things, answered saying, Nothing can prevent two (viz., decrepitude and death); nor is it true that these cannot be prevented under any circumstances.

verses.sanskrit: पञ्चयज्ञांस्तु यो मोहान्न करोति गृहाश्रमे । तस्य नायं न च परो लोको भवति धर्मतः ॥७॥
verses.english: Neither days, nor nights, nor months, cease to go on. Only that man who, though transitory, follows the eternal path succeeds in avoiding birth and death.

verses.sanskrit: तद्ब्रूहि मां सुविश्रब्धो यत्त्वं वाचा वदिष्यसि । तत्करिष्याम्यहं सर्वं मा त्वं शोके मनः कृथाः ॥८॥
verses.english: Destruction overtakes all creatures. All creatures seem to be ceaselessly borne along the endless current of time. Those that are borne along the endless current of time which is without a vessel and which in infested by those two powerful alligators, viz., decrepitude and death, sink down without anybody coming to their help.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा शकुनेर्लुब्धकोऽब्रवीत् । बाधते खलु मे शीतं संत्राणं हि विधीयताम् ॥९॥
verses.english: As one is swept along that current, one does not find any friend for help and one does not feel any interest for any one else.

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्तस्ततः पक्षी पर्णान्यास्तीर्य भूतले । यथाशक्त्या हि पर्णेन ज्वलनार्थं द्रुतं ययौ ॥१०॥
verses.english: One meets with wives and other friends only on his road. One had never before enjoyed this sort of companionship with any one for any length of time.

verses.sanskrit: स गत्वाऽङ्गारकर्मान्तं गृहीत्वाग्निमथागमत् । ततः शुष्केषु पर्णेषु पावकं सोऽप्यदीपयत् ॥११॥
verses.english: Creatures, as they are carried along the current to time, become again and again are drawn towards one another like clouds moved by the wind meeting one another with loud noise.

verses.sanskrit: स तथोक्तस्तथेत्युक्त्वा लुब्धो गात्राण्यतापयत् । अग्निं प्रत्यागतप्राणस्ततः प्राह विहङ्गमम् ॥१३॥
हर्षेण महताऽऽविष्टो वाक्यं व्याकुललोचनः । तथेमं शकुनिं दृष्ट्वा विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा ॥१४॥
दत्तमाहारमिच्छामि त्वया क्षुद्बाधते हि माम् । स तद्वचः प्रतिश्रुत्य वाक्यमाह विहङ्गमः ॥१५॥
न मेऽस्ति विभवो येन नाशयेयं क्षुधां तव । उत्पन्नेन हि जीवामो वयं नित्यं वनौकसः ॥१६॥
संचयो नास्ति चास्माकं मुनीनामिव भोजने । इत्युक्त्वा तं तदा तत्र विवर्णवदनोऽभवत् ॥१७॥
कथं न खलु कर्तव्यमिति चिन्तापरस्तदा । बभूव भरतश्रेष्ठ गर्हयन् वृत्तिमात्मनः ॥१८॥
मुहूर्ताल्लब्धसंज्ञस्तु स पक्षी पक्षिघातिनम् । उवाच तर्पयिष्ये त्वां मुहूर्तं प्रतिपालय ॥१९॥
इत्युक्त्वा शुष्कपर्णैस्तु समुज्ज्वाल्य हुताशनम् । हर्षेण महताऽऽविष्टः स पक्षी वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥२०॥
verses.english: Saying these words he lighted up a fire with the help of some dry leaves, and filled with joy, said,-I heard formerly from great Rishis, gods and Pitris that there is great merit in honouring a guest.

verses.sanskrit: ऋषीणां देवतानां च पितॄणां च महात्मनाम् । श्रुतः पूर्वं मया धर्मो महानतिथिपूजने ॥२१॥
कुरुष्वानुग्रहं सौम्य सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि ते । निश्चिता खलु मे बुद्धिरतिथिप्रतिपूजने ॥२२॥
verses.english: O amiable one, be kind to me. To tell you the truth my heart is bent upon honouring you my guest.

verses.sanskrit: ततः कृतप्रतिज्ञो वै स पक्षी प्रहसन्निव । तमग्निं त्रिःपरिक्रम्य प्रविवेश महामतिः ॥२३॥
verses.english: Having thus made up his mind, the great bird, with a smiling face, thrice went round that fire and then entered its flames.

verses.sanskrit: अग्निमध्ये प्रविष्टं तु लुब्धो दृष्ट्वा तु पक्षिणम् । चिन्तयामास मनसा किमिदं वे मया कृतम् ॥२४॥
verses.english: Seeing the bird enter that fire, the fowler began to think! and asked himself,-What have I done.

verses.sanskrit: अहो मम नृशंसस्य गर्हितस्य स्वकर्मणा । अधर्मः सुमहान् घोरो भविष्यति न संशयः ॥२५॥
verses.english: Alas, dreadful will be the sin, the outcome of my own acts. I am highly ruthless and blameable.

verses.sanskrit: एवं बहुविधं भूरि विललाप स लुब्धकः । गार्हयन्स्वानि कर्माणि द्विजं दृष्ट्वा तथागतम् ॥२६॥
verses.english: Indeed, seeing the bird lay down his life, the fowler, considering his own acts, began to bewail thus piteously.
